title: Sheaf tensor structure maps commute with unit comparisons before coherence
statement:
Let $C$ be an essentially small site and $\mathcal A$ a Grothendieck abelian category with a closed symmetric monoidal structure additive in each variable. Let $\mathrm{PSh}=\mathrm{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ have the objectwise tensor $\otimes_p$, unit $I$, associator $\alpha^p$, unitors $\lambda^p,\rho^p$, and symmetry $\beta^p$ of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf]. Let $a:\mathrm{PSh}\to\mathrm{Sh}(C,\mathcal A)$ be sheafification, $i$ the full inclusion, $\eta_P:P\to iaP$ its unit, and $\epsilon_S:aiS\to S$ the inverse of $\eta_{iS}$, using [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Write $W=\{g:a(g)\text{ is invertible}\}$; the tensor stability and unit comparisons are those of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso].

For sheaves set $F\star G=a(iF\otimes_piG)$, with $(u\star v)=a(iu\otimes_piv)$, and $J=aI$. Define the following maps, without assuming that they satisfy monoidal coherence:
$$
\alpha^\star_{F,G,H}=a(iF\otimes_p\eta_{iG\otimes_piH})\circ a(\alpha^p_{iF,iG,iH})\circ a(\eta_{iF\otimes_piG}\otimes_piH)^{-1},
$$
$$
\lambda^\star_F=\epsilon_F\circ a(\lambda^p_{iF})\circ a(\eta_I\otimes_piF)^{-1},\qquad
\rho^\star_F=\epsilon_F\circ a(\rho^p_{iF})\circ a(iF\otimes_p\eta_I)^{-1},\qquad
\beta^\star_{F,G}=a(\beta^p_{iF,iG}).
$$
For any presheaves $P,Q,R$, sheaves $F,G,H$, and arbitrary morphisms $f:P\to iF$, $g:Q\to iG$, $h:R\to iH$, put
$$d(f,g)=\eta_{iF\otimes_piG}\circ(f\otimes_pg):P\otimes_pQ\to i(F\star G).$$
Then the following four equalities hold as morphisms of presheaves:
$$
i(\alpha^\star_{F,G,H})\circ d(d(f,g),h)=d(f,d(g,h))\circ\alpha^p_{P,Q,R},
$$
$$
i(\lambda^\star_F)\circ d(\eta_I,f)=f\circ\lambda^p_P,\qquad
i(\rho^\star_F)\circ d(f,\eta_I)=f\circ\rho^p_P,
$$
$$
i(\beta^\star_{F,G})\circ d(f,g)=d(g,f)\circ\beta^p_{P,Q}.
$$

source.place: Second paragraph, first sentence (explicit four comparison identities)

proof.text: First justify all inverse maps used in the statement. For any presheaf $X$ and sheaf $T$, precomposition with $\eta_X$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(iaX,iT)\to\operatorname{Hom}(X,iT)$ by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The Hom characterization of $W$ in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso] therefore gives $\eta_X\in W$, and clause 1 gives invertibility after $a$ of $\eta_X\otimes_p\operatorname{id}_Y$ and $\operatorname{id}_Y\otimes_p\eta_X$, for every presheaf $Y$. These include all maps inverted in $\alpha^\star,\lambda^\star,\rho^\star$. For a sheaf $T$, the universal property extends $\operatorname{id}_{iT}$ to $r:aiT\to T$ with $ir\circ\eta_{iT}=\operatorname{id}_{iT}$. Both $\eta_{iT}\circ ir$ and the identity of $iaiT$ become $\eta_{iT}$ after precomposition with $\eta_{iT}$, so uniqueness in that same universal property makes them equal. Thus $r=\epsilon_T$ and $i\epsilon_T\circ\eta_{iT}=\operatorname{id}_{iT}$.

source.place: First paragraph: comparisons built from units become invertible after sheafification

proof.text:
We will use the following one-line cancellation, without any sheaf monoidal coherence. Naturality of the unit of the adjunction in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] says, for $t:X\to Y$,
$$i(a(t))\circ\eta_X=\eta_Y\circ t.$$
Indeed both sides are the adjunct of $a(t)$ under the stated universal property. When $a(t)$ is invertible, postcomposition by its inverse gives
$$i(a(t)^{-1})\circ\eta_Y\circ t=\eta_X.$$
We abbreviate $i(a(u))$ by $ia(u)$ below. These are equalities of presheaf morphisms.

source.place: Second paragraph, first sentence: natural unit comparisons and inverse cancellation

proof.text:
For the associator put $X=iF\otimes_piG$, $Y=iG\otimes_piH$, $S=X\otimes_piH$, $T=iF\otimes_pY$, $D=iaX\otimes_piH$, and $E=iF\otimes_piaY$. Write $t=\eta_X\otimes_p\operatorname{id}_{iH}:S\to D$, $v=\operatorname{id}_{iF}\otimes_p\eta_Y:T\to E$, and $k=(f\otimes_pg)\otimes_ph$. Bifunctoriality of the objectwise tensor of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf] expands
$$d(d(f,g),h)=\eta_D\circ t\circ k.$$
The inverse $a(t)^{-1}$ exists by step 1 and [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso]. Substitute the definition of $\alpha^\star$, cancel using step 2, and apply unit naturality to $v\circ\alpha^p_{iF,iG,iH}$:
$$
 i\alpha^\star\circ\eta_D\circ t\circ k
 =ia(v)\circ ia(\alpha^p_{iF,iG,iH})\circ\eta_S\circ k
 =\eta_E\circ v\circ\alpha^p_{iF,iG,iH}\circ k.
$$
Naturality of the presheaf associator gives
$$\alpha^p_{iF,iG,iH}\circ k=(f\otimes_p(g\otimes_ph))\circ\alpha^p_{P,Q,R}.$$
Thus the last displayed expression equals
$$\eta_E\circ(f\otimes_p(\eta_Y\circ(g\otimes_ph)))\circ\alpha^p_{P,Q,R}
=d(f,d(g,h))\circ\alpha^p_{P,Q,R},$$
as required. Only the presheaf associator's naturality is used.

source.place: Second paragraph, first sentence: associator is conjugate by the unit comparisons

proof.text:
For the left unitor put $t=\eta_I\otimes_p\operatorname{id}_{iF}:I\otimes_piF\to iaI\otimes_piF$, $D=iaI\otimes_piF$, and $k=\operatorname{id}_I\otimes_pf$. By tensor bifunctoriality,
$$d(\eta_I,f)=\eta_D\circ t\circ k.$$
The tensor stability in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso] justifies the inverse in the following calculation. Steps 1 and 2 and unit naturality for $\lambda^p_{iF}$ give
$$
 i\lambda^\star_F\circ d(\eta_I,f)
 =i\epsilon_F\circ ia(\lambda^p_{iF})\circ\eta_{I\otimes_piF}\circ k
 =i\epsilon_F\circ\eta_{iF}\circ\lambda^p_{iF}\circ k
 =\lambda^p_{iF}\circ(\operatorname{id}_I\otimes_pf).
$$
Naturality of the presheaf left unitor in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf] identifies the last expression with $f\circ\lambda^p_P$. This proves the left-unitor equality for arbitrary $f$.

source.place: Second paragraph, first sentence: left unitor and the unit comparison

proof.text:
For the right unitor put $t=\operatorname{id}_{iF}\otimes_p\eta_I:iF\otimes_pI\to iF\otimes_piaI$, $D=iF\otimes_piaI$, and $k=f\otimes_p\operatorname{id}_I$. Then
$$d(f,\eta_I)=\eta_D\circ t\circ k.$$
Here too $a(t)$ is invertible by [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso]. Substitute $\rho^\star_F$ and use steps 1 and 2:
$$
 i\rho^\star_F\circ d(f,\eta_I)
 =i\epsilon_F\circ ia(\rho^p_{iF})\circ\eta_{iF\otimes_pI}\circ k
 =i\epsilon_F\circ\eta_{iF}\circ\rho^p_{iF}\circ k
 =\rho^p_{iF}\circ(f\otimes_p\operatorname{id}_I)
 =f\circ\rho^p_P.
$$
The middle equality is unit naturality for $\rho^p_{iF}$ followed by $i\epsilon_F\circ\eta_{iF}=\operatorname{id}$; the final equality is naturality of the presheaf right unitor in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf].

source.place: Second paragraph, first sentence: right unitor and the unit comparison

proof.text:
Finally put $X=iF\otimes_piG$ and $Y=iG\otimes_piF$. By the definition of $\beta^\star$, unit naturality from step 2, and naturality of the presheaf symmetry in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf],
$$
 i\beta^\star_{F,G}\circ d(f,g)
 =ia(\beta^p_{iF,iG})\circ\eta_X\circ(f\otimes_pg)
 =\eta_Y\circ\beta^p_{iF,iG}\circ(f\otimes_pg)
 =\eta_Y\circ(g\otimes_pf)\circ\beta^p_{P,Q}
 =d(g,f)\circ\beta^p_{P,Q}.
$$
This proves the fourth equality directly. None of the six steps assumes coherence, naturality, or functorial monoidality of the proposed sheaf structure maps.

source.place: Second paragraph, first sentence: symmetry induced by the objectwise symmetry
